summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.16/700)

data.turoyo: ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Lo lo bu arʕo di nuqro qayse latwo, bəṯr maqəṯiwo nuro w annaqqa mḥalqiwo, kətwole lu atuno tre tarʕe, ḥa mi xaṣrayo w ḥa mayo. Annaqqe tre gəd maḥtiwo, hən mnawliwonne, mḥalqiwo hama, təfkiwo bah hno.... Kətwolle hawxa xəd u hno, xəd am mədone ḥadid wayye...
data.translation: Uncle Isho: No, no, there was no wood on the floor of the pit. Afterwards they would light a fire and then throw it in. The kiln had two doors, one at its side and one on top. Then two people would put it in; if they passed it to them, they would throw that in, push it with that.... They had something like that, like poles, they were iron...

rationale: First Infectum-wa cell; passing fuel to kiln workers. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation; the Turoyo determines the sense.

summary: New sense 1b: einander angreifen, Schläge wechseln (mit b-ḥḏoḏe; b-: Waffe)

data.label: 1b
data.gloss: einander angreifen, Schläge wechseln (mit b-ḥḏoḏe; b-: Waffe)

rationale: Reciprocal b ḥḏoḏe plus swords describes mutual combat followed by an actual sword blow; this specializes directed transfer rather than simple hand-to-hand passing. One clear attestation.

data.turoyo: <...> Qayəm, mnawalle b ḥḏoḏe bas sayfe. <...>
data.translation: <...> Der Riese erhob sich und sie griffen einander mit den Schwertern an. <...>

rationale: First example of the new reciprocal combat construction; complete coordinated sentence.

data.turoyo: <...> ḥəngi d ftəḥḥe u syoġo, babi nafəq bu šəbbak bi xərbayo w mnawəlalle emi, uno w ḥoṯi <...>
data.translation: <...> when they opened the wall, my father went out through the window in those ruins, and they passed my mother, me and my sister to him. <...>

rationale: Thin Preterit sense-1 cell has one after round 1; human patients and recipient contrast with the pencil. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation; the Turoyo determines the sense.

summary: New idiom: mnawele/mnawəl iḏo 'die Hand ausstrecken'

data.turoyo: <...> Mnaweli iḏi hawxa, mdaqro. Aṯi kefo rabṯo qumi. <...>
data.translation: <...> I reached out my hand like this, bracing myself. A big stone came in front of me. <...>

rationale: One clear body-part collocation: hand is extended rather than transferred to a recipient. Search mnaw and iḏo found no matching nwl collocation; the ftḥ hand-holding-out expression is a different verb. Supplied English is project machine translation; interpretation rests on the Turoyo.

summary: The reciprocal participant relation and the weapon both use b-, but have different roles: b ḥḏoḏe identifies opponents and bas sayfe the means of attack.
Plural Preterit mnawalle is retained under II. It introduces mutual combat, with the following feminine sword-blow clause confirming a violent exchange.
A construction subsense preserves inherited label 1 and its pencil example. No second idiom listing or unrelated general sense 'fight' is added.
mnawəlalle codes plural agents and a recipient alongside overt human patients. mnawəlileyo has an object/recipient chain, but exact suffix boundaries need confirmation.
mnawliwonne supplies the first Infectum-wa of ordinary transfer. No example supports or overturns round-1 reciprocal combat subsense 1b.

The overt hand in Mnaweli iḏi is the extended body part. Record it once as a collocation; it is not an abstract light-verb construction and does not require general reach as a separate numbered sense. Read-only glossary searches mnaw and iḏo were checked before adding it.
